answer: A farm running 39 keys as a result burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the tundra stake is held until the relic settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the zephyr audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 8% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
